# k3d_config_map (Resource)

A Kubernetes ConfigMap. Creating one that already exists fails: import it instead. Import with `<cluster>/<namespace>/<name>`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "k3d_config_map" "settings" {
  cluster   = k3d_cluster.main.id
  namespace = k3d_namespace.app.name
  name      = "settings"

  data = {
    LOG_LEVEL = "info"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) ConfigMap name.

### Optional

- `annotations` (Map of String) Annotations. Only keys set here are tracked, so ones added by controllers do not show as changes.
- `cluster` (String) Cluster to manage the object in, usually `k3d_cluster.<name>.id`, so the object is recreated when the cluster is replaced. Exactly one of `cluster` or `kubeconfig` is required.
- `data` (Map of String) Keys and values. Only keys set here are tracked.
- `kubeconfig` (String, Sensitive) Kubeconfig contents, for a cluster that is reached directly and not through Docker. Not recorded as a dependency on the cluster's lifetime, so prefer `cluster` for clusters in the same configuration. It is stored in Terraform state, so use an encrypted state backend.
- `labels` (Map of String) Labels. Only keys set here are tracked, so ones added by controllers do not show as changes.
- `namespace` (String) Namespace of the object. Defaults to `default`.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) `<cluster>/<namespace>/<name>`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import k3d_config_map.settings demo/app/settings
```
